primary_topics: Interview responses by CJP about the origin and legacy of the Manila Cathedral coffee table book -- 'Restoring a Monument to Faith, Architecture and History' -- published March 9, 2019

The origin story of the Cathedral restoration: Cardinal Rosales summoning the Foundation to address the swaying belfry in 2010; the discovery of no as-built plans anywhere; Cardinal Tagle's decision to close the Cathedral for structural safety
How the coffee table book was funded: Metrobank Foundation's budget exhausted; referral to GT Foundation; Alfred Ty personally delivering the check
The book's transformation from a technical record into a 'world-class, grand coffee table book' that is both a legacy document for future restorers and a testament to faith and religious heritage
sub_topics: Question 1 -- How the idea started: CJP as President of the Manila Metropolitan Cathedral-Basilica Foundation; Cardinal Rosales' summons to address the swaying belfry (swayed when cargo trucks passed); structural engineers found not just the belfry but the entire edifice needed strengthening

The absent as-built plans: no architectural designs, structural plans found anywhere -- not in Archdiocese archives, National Library, Manila City Engineer's Office; no one knew what pilings or rock the Cathedral stood on
Reclaimed land risk: structural engineers warned the Cathedral was built on reclaimed land which 'could liquefy and cause the Cathedral to collapse'

Cardinal Tagle's closure decision: after receiving the structural engineers' written report, CJP advised (with others) that Cardinal Tagle should close the Cathedral to avoid potential liability for deaths or damage; Tagle's 'first major decision' was to close it
Completion of the four Rs: strengthening, retrofitting, renovating the Cathedral -- with guidance of the Lord and the help of Our Lady of the Immaculate Conception

The book proposal: CJP proposed publishing a coffee table book to document the restoration with structural and architectural plans -- 'so that 50 years or 100 years from now... future generations... will no longer meet the same baffling problems we faced'

Funding solution: Board of Trustees (chaired by Cardinal Tagle; vice-chaired by Ambassador Tita de Villa) welcomed the proposal; Metrobank Foundation had exhausted its budget; referred to sister GT Foundation; Alfred Ty 'gallantly and kindly agreed at short notice to issue the check' and 'delivered the check today'

Book's transformation: Dr. Gerald Lico tasked with design and editing; the book 'metamorphosed into a world-class, grand coffee table book' distributed to Catholic personalities and offices in the Philippines and worldwide

Question 2 -- Legacy: 'More than brick and mortar, the Manila Cathedral is a symbol of our deep faith and a monument of our religious heritage as a people... the coffee table book is a testament not just to the herculean effort to restore, re-strengthen, retrofit and beautify the mortar and brick... but it is now also a witness to the architectural and historical genius of our faithful in their adoration of our Lord and in their veneration of our Lady'

one_paragraph_summary: Published March 9, 2019 as interview responses by CJP about the Manila Cathedral coffee table book ('Restoring a Monument to Faith, Architecture and History'), this document covers two questions. On how the idea started: the restoration of the Manila Cathedral began in 2010 when Cardinal Rosales summoned the Manila Metropolitan Cathedral-Basilica Foundation (CJP as President) to address the swaying belfry; structural engineers found not just the belfry but the entire edifice needed strengthening; and to CJP's dismay, no as-built plans were found anywhere (not in Archdiocese archives, the National Library, or the Manila City Engineer's Office), with the additional alarm that the Cathedral was built on reclaimed land that 'could liquefy and cause the Cathedral to collapse.' When Cardinal Tagle succeeded Rosales, CJP advised him (with others) that closing the Cathedral was legally necessary to avoid liability should it collapse -- making it Tagle's first major decision as Archbishop. After the four Rs were completed with the Lord's guidance, CJP proposed a coffee table book to document the restoration with structural and architectural plans -- 'so that 50 years or 100 years from now, future generations who may wish to re-strengthen, retrofit and re-beautify the Cathedral will no longer meet the same baffling problems we faced.' The Board (chaired by Cardinal Tagle, vice-chaired by Ambassador Tita de Villa) welcomed the proposal; Metrobank Foundation had exhausted its budget; referred it to the GT Foundation; Alfred Ty 'gallantly and kindly agreed at short notice' and personally delivered the check on the day of the interview. Under Dr. Gerald Lico's design and editing, the book 'metamorphosed into a world-class, grand coffee table book' distributed worldwide. On the book's legacy: 'More than brick and mortar, the Manila Cathedral is a symbol of our deep faith and a monument of our religious heritage as a people... the coffee table book is a testament not just to the herculean effort to restore... but a witness to the architectural and historical genius of our faithful in their adoration of our Lord and in their veneration of our Lady.'
